world.title: Vance demands Iran cut uranium enrichment for deal to end war
world.summary: U.S. Vice President JD Vance said Iran must make a meaningful, concrete reduction in its uranium-enrichment capacity before Washington would agree to end the seven-month war. He rejected promises of future limits as insufficient. He questioned Iran’s use of uranium enriched to 60% and said the United States remained op
world.content: U.S. Vice President JD Vance said Iran must make a meaningful, concrete reduction in its uranium-enrichment capacity before Washington would agree to end the seven-month war. He rejected promises of future limits as insufficient. He questioned Iran’s use of uranium enriched to 60% and said the United States remained open to a deal but would not accept words in place of action. The United States and Iran have exchanged proposals in recent weeks to stop the fighting and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for energy shipments. President Donald Trump rejected Tehran’s latest offer and warned that military operations could intensify after November’s midterm elections. Vance said U.S. officials are negotiating with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi but do not know how much authority they hold. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei disputed that account, saying contradictory statements from Washington were the problem. Vance said Trump is directing U.S. policy on the conflict.

world.title: Belgian-American physicist Francis Halzen wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics
world.summary: Belgian-American physicist Francis Halzen won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics on Oct. 6 for his decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos from astrophysical sources. The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences said the observatory’s measurements can show how high-en
world.content: Belgian-American physicist Francis Halzen won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics on Oct. 6 for his decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos from astrophysical sources. The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences said the observatory’s measurements can show how high-energy neutrinos are produced and may reveal previously unknown cosmic phenomena. Halzen’s project turned a cubic kilometer of Antarctic ice into a detector, with thousands of sensors designed to record faint flashes created when neutrinos collide with matter. The particles can travel vast distances without being deflected by magnetic fields, helping researchers trace them to distant cosmic sources. Halzen said the scientific possibilities remain unknown and that neutrino astronomy will require larger and more numerous detectors. A planned IceCube-Gen2 expansion covering eight cubic kilometers is expected to begin operating in 2033; the Nobel award ceremony is scheduled for Dec. 10 in Stockholm.

world.title: Drones sink Togo-flagged cargo ship off Bulgaria, crew missing
world.summary: Drones struck two commercial ships in Bulgaria’s Black Sea exclusive economic zone early Oct. 6, sinking the Togo-flagged Alfa Watan and setting the Palau-flagged Able on fire, Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said. Rescuers saved 18 crew members from the Able, two of whom were injured. The Alfa Watan’s crew remain
world.content: Drones struck two commercial ships in Bulgaria’s Black Sea exclusive economic zone early Oct. 6, sinking the Togo-flagged Alfa Watan and setting the Palau-flagged Able on fire, Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said. Rescuers saved 18 crew members from the Able, two of whom were injured. The Alfa Watan’s crew remained missing as Bulgarian authorities searched about 70 nautical miles east of Byala. Both vessels were identified as Turkish-owned, and the Able was carrying grain. Radev said the drones’ origin had not been established and condemned the attack as a violation of maritime law. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said a joint investigation with Bulgaria’s navy attributed the strike to Russia; Moscow had not commented at the time of the reports. A maritime-security source cited by Reuters said preliminary assessments indicated a likely Russian attack. Bulgarian authorities continued the search operation and checked for possible environmental damage. The incident followed a ship fire off Romania on Oct. 5; authorities had not publicly confirmed its cause.
world.image_alt: Drones sink Togo-flagged cargo ship off Bulgaria, crew missing

world.title: Russian missile and drone barrage kills two in Kyiv, strikes other cities
world.summary: Russian forces launched a large missile-and-drone attack across Ukraine overnight on Oct. 7, killing at least two people in Kyiv and damaging civilian sites in several cities, Ukrainian officials said. Kyiv officials reported fires and damage in multiple districts. Strikes also damaged an industrial facility in Dnipro,
world.content: Russian forces launched a large missile-and-drone attack across Ukraine overnight on Oct. 7, killing at least two people in Kyiv and damaging civilian sites in several cities, Ukrainian officials said. Kyiv officials reported fires and damage in multiple districts. Strikes also damaged an industrial facility in Dnipro, transport infrastructure in Zaporizhzhia and apartment buildings in Kremenchuk. DW, citing regional authorities, reported that four people were killed in Pryluky and two in Kremenchuk, where seven others were injured. The attack followed President Volodymyr Zelensky’s warning on Oct. 6 that intelligence indicated Russia was preparing a large-scale assault. He urged residents to heed air-raid alerts and asked Ukraine’s partners, particularly the United States and Europe, to provide defensive capabilities. Russia’s Defence Ministry said it targeted military-industrial facilities, port infrastructure and vessels it said served Ukraine’s armed forces. Poland scrambled military aircraft and raised its air-defence and radar readiness during the attack.
world.image_alt: Russian missile and drone barrage kills two in Kyiv, strikes other cities

world.title: UK police make seventh arrest in suspected RAF Fairford plot
world.summary: British police arrested a 22-year-old man in Westminster on Oct. 6 on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts, the seventh arrest in an investigation into a suspected plot at RAF Fairford, an air base used by U.S. bombers. The other six suspects, including a dual British-Iranian national, have been released on bail; no o
world.content: British police arrested a 22-year-old man in Westminster on Oct. 6 on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts, the seventh arrest in an investigation into a suspected plot at RAF Fairford, an air base used by U.S. bombers. The other six suspects, including a dual British-Iranian national, have been released on bail; no one has been charged. The investigation began after five men were detained near the base on Sept. 27. Police said three vans linked to the suspects contained gasoline but no explosives. Residents near the base were evacuated during the response. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has cited “strong indications” of an Iranian role, while Tehran denies involvement. The U.S. moved its bombers from Fairford to their home bases on Oct. 4. U.S. officials cited by Reuters said concern about a possible Iranian drone attack prompted the move. President Trump said a threat linked to Iran was involved but gave no details. British police say their inquiry continues.
world.image_alt: UK police make seventh arrest in suspected RAF Fairford plot

world.title: Trump says Iran could strike Los Angeles, San Diego, prompting backlash
world.summary: President Donald Trump said at a Nebraska rally on Oct. 5 that Iran could “take out” Los Angeles or San Diego. He called such a loss a “small price to pay” for keeping the country safe as he defended the Iran war and higher fuel and fertilizer costs. His comments drew criticism from California officials and some Republ
world.content: President Donald Trump said at a Nebraska rally on Oct. 5 that Iran could “take out” Los Angeles or San Diego. He called such a loss a “small price to pay” for keeping the country safe as he defended the Iran war and higher fuel and fertilizer costs. His comments drew criticism from California officials and some Republicans. The White House said he was warning that a nuclear-armed Iran would threaten U.S. cities, not inviting an attack. California Gov. Gavin Newsom ordered the state’s threat assessment center to monitor whether foreign actors might interpret Trump’s remarks as an invitation to target the state. Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass and San Diego Mayor Todd Gloria also objected; Republican congressional candidate Jim Desmond said no U.S. city should be treated as expendable. Trump said the war was “essentially almost over” and would end soon, but gave no timeline. Early voting is beginning in California, and Republicans are seeking to defend their congressional majorities in November’s midterm elections.
world.image_alt: Trump says Iran could strike Los Angeles, San Diego, prompting backlash

world.title: Russia says drone attack set Liberian-flagged oil tanker ablaze off Sochi
world.summary: A Liberian-flagged oil tanker caught fire off Russia’s Black Sea resort city of Sochi on Tuesday after what Russia’s Transport Ministry said was an attack by unmanned boats. All 23 crew members, who were Indian nationals, were rescued. The ministry said crude oil was burning on the water and the blaze was initially too
world.content: A Liberian-flagged oil tanker caught fire off Russia’s Black Sea resort city of Sochi on Tuesday after what Russia’s Transport Ministry said was an attack by unmanned boats. All 23 crew members, who were Indian nationals, were rescued. The ministry said crude oil was burning on the water and the blaze was initially too intense for firefighting vessels to approach. Ukraine has not commented on the tanker incident. Authorities closed beaches in the nearby Sirius area and monitored air and water quality. Russian officials said pollutant levels in the area remained below permitted limits. Monitoring of the fire and potential marine pollution continued. The incident followed separate drone strikes on two merchant ships in Bulgaria’s Black Sea exclusive economic zone: one sank and the other caught fire. Bulgaria said it was investigating the drones’ origin. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy blamed Russia for those attacks, but no one claimed responsibility. Russia’s Transport Ministry said firefighting would begin once the blaze subsided enough for rescue vessels to approach safely.
world.image_alt: Russia says drone attack set Liberian-flagged oil tanker ablaze off Sochi

world.title: Germany arrests former BND chief over alleged sale of state secrets
world.summary: German authorities arrested former foreign intelligence chief August Hanning on Tuesday on suspicion of espionage, treason and obtaining state secrets. Hanning, 80, led the Federal Intelligence Service, or BND, from 1998 to 2005. Authorities also arrested a former aide, identified as Manfred D., on suspicion of helping
world.content: German authorities arrested former foreign intelligence chief August Hanning on Tuesday on suspicion of espionage, treason and obtaining state secrets. Hanning, 80, led the Federal Intelligence Service, or BND, from 1998 to 2005. Authorities also arrested a former aide, identified as Manfred D., on suspicion of helping him. Federal prosecutors allege that Hanning and Manfred D. agreed in 2010 that the aide would provide classified intelligence in exchange for payment. They say Manfred D. supplied about 2,000 documents over several years and that Hanning used the information in private consulting work, including to prepare an analysis for a foreign intelligence officer. Prosecutors have not identified the foreign services involved and say it is unclear whether the analysis reached its intended recipient. The investigation began after investigators found evidence during a search of Hanning’s home in a separate case in 2025. Federal prosecutors opened a covert investigation in May 2026. Some material reportedly came from senior-level briefings that included information from partner agencies. Both suspects were expected to appear before a judge.
world.image_alt: Germany arrests former BND chief over alleged sale of state secrets

business.title: Judge weighs Disney bid to halt FCC
business.summary: A federal judge on Tuesday heard arguments on Disney and ABC’s request to block the Federal Communications Commission from accelerating license renewal reviews for eight ABC-owned stations, whose licenses were not due to expire until between 2028 and 2031. Disney says the process retaliates against the network’s covera
business.content: A federal judge on Tuesday heard arguments on Disney and ABC’s request to block the Federal Communications Commission from accelerating license renewal reviews for eight ABC-owned stations, whose licenses were not due to expire until between 2028 and 2031. Disney says the process retaliates against the network’s coverage and risks chilling editorial decisions; the FCC says it is seeking information in an investigation of Disney’s employment practices and argues the case belongs in a different court. U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan did not rule after the hearing and questioned why the FCC chose to review all eight stations early and whether other investigative tools were available. Six of the stations operate in major media markets and contribute significantly to ABC’s bottom line. The government must file additional arguments by Oct. 9 and ABC by Oct. 14; a ruling was not expected before mid-October.
business.image_alt: Judge weighs Disney bid to halt FCC

business.title: India
business.summary: The Reserve Bank of India raised its benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5% on Oct. 7, its first increase since February 2023, and shifted its policy stance from neutral to “calibrated tightening”. Governor Sanjay Malhotra said rate cuts were off the table in the near term; future action would be a hike or a pa
business.content: The Reserve Bank of India raised its benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5% on Oct. 7, its first increase since February 2023, and shifted its policy stance from neutral to “calibrated tightening”. Governor Sanjay Malhotra said rate cuts were off the table in the near term; future action would be a hike or a pause depending on conditions. The decision followed August retail inflation of 4.82%, above the RBI’s 4% medium-term target for a third consecutive month, with price pressures spreading beyond food and transport. The central bank cited higher energy costs linked to the Middle East conflict, rupee weakness and risks to food prices from weak monsoon rains. Crude oil was around $100 a barrel, while India’s April-June GDP growth reached 7.8%. The RBI raised its FY27 inflation forecast to 5.2% and its growth forecast to 7.1%, from 6.7% previously. Economists see further tightening as possible, but the central bank said the course will depend on how inflation and growth evolve.

business.title: ECB official says France does not meet conditions for bond-market intervention
business.summary: European Central Bank Governing Council member Emmanuel Moulin said France has not met the conditions for ECB intervention in its bond market, describing the situation as serious and complicated. He said France must address its public finances rather than rely on central bank support. French 10-year borrowing costs hav
business.content: European Central Bank Governing Council member Emmanuel Moulin said France has not met the conditions for ECB intervention in its bond market, describing the situation as serious and complicated. He said France must address its public finances rather than rely on central bank support. French 10-year borrowing costs have approached 5%, their highest level since 2002, as investors weigh persistent deficits, political uncertainty and the government’s ability to secure savings measures. France’s public debt is close to 120% of GDP, while its deficit has remained above 5% in recent years. The government has proposed a 2027 budget package with €43 billion in savings and tax increases, but opposition parties are expected to challenge measures including a freeze on some public-sector pay. France also plans to issue a record €340 billion in government bonds in 2027.
business.image_alt: ECB official says France does not meet conditions for bond-market intervention

business.title: ASOS investigates customer data exposure after hackers hijack app alerts
business.summary: ASOS said it is investigating unauthorized access involving third-party platforms used to communicate with customers after hackers sent an “ASOS HACKED” push notification through its app on Oct. 6, threatening to leak data and directing users to Telegram. The retailer said names and contact details may have been access
business.content: ASOS said it is investigating unauthorized access involving third-party platforms used to communicate with customers after hackers sent an “ASOS HACKED” push notification through its app on Oct. 6, threatening to leak data and directing users to Telegram. The retailer said names and contact details may have been accessed, but it does not believe payment-card information or account passwords were affected. ASOS said it restricted access to the notification platforms and apologized to customers. The website and app continued operating normally, ASOS said, and the company has cybersecurity and business-continuity insurance; it cautioned that it was too early to quantify any effect on trading. Shares fell more than 14% during the day and closed down 9.56%. Snowflake said its investigation had found no compromise of its platform so far, leaving the attackers’ claim that they accessed an ASOS Snowflake instance unverified. ASOS is working with specialists and relevant authorities, and the UK’s National Cyber Security Centre offered assistance. The Information Commissioner’s Office said it did not appear to have received a report at that stage. ASOS has not disclosed how many customers may be affected or the full scope of potentially accessed information, and said it would provide updates as the investigation progresses.
business.image_alt: ASOS investigates customer data exposure after hackers hijack app alerts

business.title: French school protests draw 256,000, intensifying pressure over public spending
business.summary: A total of 256,000 people joined demonstrations across France on Tuesday, including 56,000 in Paris, as students, teachers and parents demanded more funding for schools. Police fired tear gas, and in some cities used water cannons to disperse violent groups; small groups clashed with officers in Paris during a largely
business.content: A total of 256,000 people joined demonstrations across France on Tuesday, including 56,000 in Paris, as students, teachers and parents demanded more funding for schools. Police fired tear gas, and in some cities used water cannons to disperse violent groups; small groups clashed with officers in Paris during a largely peaceful march. The protests have grown from demonstrations that began at a high school in the Paris region in mid-September, adding pressure on a government trying to curb public spending while meeting demands for core services. Students cite teacher shortages, poorly maintained classrooms and inadequate resources. The Education Ministry said classes were fully or partly suspended at 891 schools on Tuesday, and the ministry opened an online portal for students to submit concerns anonymously. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said the government and school leaders must listen and find solutions; officials have also been told to assess repairs at ageing schools and submit initial proposals by the end of October.
business.image_alt: French school protests draw 256,000, intensifying pressure over public spending

business.title: U.S. trade deficit surges to $105.6 billion in August
business.summary: The U.S. goods and services trade deficit widened 13.7% in August to $105.6 billion, up $12.7 billion from July's revised $92.8 billion and its highest level since March 2025, the Commerce Department said Oct. 6. The monthly gap exceeded economists' $102 billion forecast. Imports climbed 4.3% to a record $420.8 billion
business.content: The U.S. goods and services trade deficit widened 13.7% in August to $105.6 billion, up $12.7 billion from July's revised $92.8 billion and its highest level since March 2025, the Commerce Department said Oct. 6. The monthly gap exceeded economists' $102 billion forecast. Imports climbed 4.3% to a record $420.8 billion, while exports rose 1.4% to $315.2 billion. Larger purchases of industrial supplies, including oil and nonmonetary gold, and capital goods such as semiconductors and machinery drove the increase; reports also linked higher technology-related imports to investment in artificial-intelligence infrastructure. The deficit for January through August was 19.9% lower than in the same period of 2025, as exports grew faster than imports.
business.image_alt: U.S. trade deficit surges to $105.6 billion in August

business.title: Emmy Awards to stream free on Amazon’s Prime Video starting in 2027
business.summary: The Television Academy has signed a six-year deal giving Amazon’s Prime Video exclusive rights to stream the Emmy Awards from 2027 through 2032, ending the ceremony’s long run on U.S. broadcast television. The awards will stream live worldwide for free, with no Prime subscription required; the 2027 ceremony remains sch
business.content: The Television Academy has signed a six-year deal giving Amazon’s Prime Video exclusive rights to stream the Emmy Awards from 2027 through 2032, ending the ceremony’s long run on U.S. broadcast television. The awards will stream live worldwide for free, with no Prime subscription required; the 2027 ceremony remains scheduled for September. El País reported that the deal would cost Amazon about $15 million a year. The agreement replaces the rotation among ABC, CBS, Fox and NBC, which have taken turns airing the ceremony for roughly three decades. Television Academy chairman Cris Abrego said a single partner would let the organization develop the telecast from year to year. The Academy also valued Prime Video’s international reach. The Emmys’ viewership has fallen to around 7 million from more than 20 million at its peak. Amazon says it plans to promote nominated shows to its customers throughout the year. The 79th Primetime Emmy Awards will be the first ceremony under the new agreement in September 2027.
business.image_alt: Emmy Awards to stream free on Amazon’s Prime Video starting in 2027

business.title: Shipowners offer tanker captains $100,000 a month amid Hormuz attacks
business.summary: Shipowners are offering tanker captains about $100,000 a month plus a $50,000 bonus for each passage through the Strait of Hormuz as Iranian attacks increase the risks of transporting Gulf oil. Ordinary crew members can earn four to six times their normal pay for Hormuz voyages, while captains typically earn about $15,
business.content: Shipowners are offering tanker captains about $100,000 a month plus a $50,000 bonus for each passage through the Strait of Hormuz as Iranian attacks increase the risks of transporting Gulf oil. Ordinary crew members can earn four to six times their normal pay for Hormuz voyages, while captains typically earn about $15,000 a month. The International Maritime Organization says at least 93 vessels have been attacked since Feb. 28 and 24 seafarers have been killed. On Oct. 4, just 13 ships crossed the strait, compared with 24 on the same day a week earlier. Tanker freight rates reached a record $1.3 million a day this week, compared with roughly $20,000 to $50,000 a day last year. Operators are using shuttle tankers to move oil through the dangerous stretch and transfer it to other vessels outside the Gulf, while many ships follow a route near Oman with U.S. air-defense support. UK Maritime Trade Operations recorded nine attacks in the waterway in October, and traders and analysts are monitoring whether the recent escalation will reduce oil and gas flows.
business.image_alt: Shipowners offer tanker captains $100,000 a month amid Hormuz attacks

science.title: Swiss glacier melt exposes artifacts; Tibetan ice may be more than 128,000 years old
science.summary: Melting Swiss glaciers are exposing ancient artifacts once trapped in ice. Switzerland has lost almost 20% of its ice in five years. Separately, researchers studying ice cores from Tibet’s Guliya ice cap say its oldest ice may be more than 128,000 years old. The Tibetan study compared cores drilled in 1992 and 2015 and
science.content: Melting Swiss glaciers are exposing ancient artifacts once trapped in ice. Switzerland has lost almost 20% of its ice in five years. Separately, researchers studying ice cores from Tibet’s Guliya ice cap say its oldest ice may be more than 128,000 years old. The Tibetan study compared cores drilled in 1992 and 2015 and used radioactive isotopes to link the chronology to a geomagnetic event more than 41,000 years ago. The team plans to analyze additional samples to place other climate indicators on the revised timeline.
science.image_alt: Swiss glacier melt exposes artifacts; Tibetan ice may be more than 128,000 years old

science.title: Bangkok floods kill 31 as extreme rainfall overwhelms drainage
science.summary: Flooding in Bangkok has killed at least 31 people and forced thousands to evacuate after about 300 millimeters of rain fell in 48 hours, overwhelming drainage systems and prompting authorities to declare a citywide disaster zone. September normally brings about 344 millimeters of rain to the capital over 18 rainy days.
science.content: Flooding in Bangkok has killed at least 31 people and forced thousands to evacuate after about 300 millimeters of rain fell in 48 hours, overwhelming drainage systems and prompting authorities to declare a citywide disaster zone. September normally brings about 344 millimeters of rain to the capital over 18 rainy days. A low-pressure system stalled over the region for about three days, sustaining the downpour. Sea-surface temperatures in the nearby Gulf of Thailand were close to 30°C. Researchers say it is too early to determine climate change’s role in this event, although studies indicate that Bangkok’s wettest day each year has been growing wetter.
science.image_alt: Bangkok floods kill 31 as extreme rainfall overwhelms drainage

science.title: X-ray study overturns 40-year assumption about cuprate superconductors
science.summary: Researchers have found that cuprate superconductors, long assumed to have a uniform crystal structure, instead contain a patchwork of different atomic arrangements, challenging a model used for four decades. The study examined LESCO, a copper-based ceramic, and was published in Physical Review Letters. The newly observ
science.content: Researchers have found that cuprate superconductors, long assumed to have a uniform crystal structure, instead contain a patchwork of different atomic arrangements, challenging a model used for four decades. The study examined LESCO, a copper-based ceramic, and was published in Physical Review Letters. The newly observed boundaries between structures are unusually wide and may hinder superconductivity rather than simply coexist with it, researcher Mark Senn said. The team plans to examine other cuprates to test whether similar structural complexity helps explain differences in their superconducting behavior.
science.image_alt: X-ray study overturns 40-year assumption about cuprate superconductors

science.title: Albanese warns Australia faces floods, cyclones and extreme heat
science.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese warned at a Pacific climate summit in Fiji on Oct. 6 that Australia could face floods, cyclones and extreme heat this summer, as forecasters anticipate a strong “super El Niño”. The meeting’s ministerial statement urged countries to deepen and accelerate emissions cuts to limi
science.content: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese warned at a Pacific climate summit in Fiji on Oct. 6 that Australia could face floods, cyclones and extreme heat this summer, as forecasters anticipate a strong “super El Niño”. The meeting’s ministerial statement urged countries to deepen and accelerate emissions cuts to limit any overshoot of the Paris Agreement’s 1.5C warming goal, warning that every additional fraction of warming increases climate impacts and the risk of irreversible loss and damage. The warning followed a visit by regional and international leaders to Tuvalu, where officials pressed for faster access to climate adaptation finance. Tuvalu Prime Minister Feleti Teo said island nations should not have to take on more debt to protect themselves from a crisis they did little to cause. The preparatory summit precedes COP31, scheduled for Turkey in November.
science.image_alt: Albanese warns Australia faces floods, cyclones and extreme heat

science.title: OpenAI posts 722 AI-generated math manuscripts from unreleased model
science.summary: OpenAI has posted 722 mathematical manuscripts generated by an unreleased internal model, organizing them into 372 families of related results in a public GitHub repository. The company says it tested the model on about 4,000 open research problems; producing most results required an average of roughly three hours of C
science.content: OpenAI has posted 722 mathematical manuscripts generated by an unreleased internal model, organizing them into 372 families of related results in a public GitHub repository. The company says it tested the model on about 4,000 open research problems; producing most results required an average of roughly three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute. The collection spans algebra, number theory, combinatorics and theoretical computer science. The manuscripts are at different stages of verification: many, but not all, include Lean formalizations that allow computers to check proof steps, and OpenAI warns that some results without formalizations could contain errors. Twenty-five Fields Medalists criticized AI companies for using open problems to test models without giving equal attention to mathematical understanding, attribution and training future researchers. OpenAI says it will fund workshops and conferences and is working to release the model responsibly, but has not announced a release date.
science.image_alt: OpenAI posts 722 AI-generated math manuscripts from unreleased model

science.title: Webb reveals young stars carving gas cavities in NGC 7129
science.summary: NASA and ESA released a James Webb Space Telescope image of NGC 7129, a star-forming region about 3,300 light-years from Earth, revealing stars and protostars obscured by dust. Webb’s infrared sensitivity reveals gas and dust structures associated with jets and outflows from young stars. The image shows outflows compre
science.content: NASA and ESA released a James Webb Space Telescope image of NGC 7129, a star-forming region about 3,300 light-years from Earth, revealing stars and protostars obscured by dust. Webb’s infrared sensitivity reveals gas and dust structures associated with jets and outflows from young stars. The image shows outflows compressing and heating surrounding gas while blowing other material away. Astronomers plan to use the Webb data to study how the stars affect the region’s gas and dust.
science.image_alt: Webb reveals young stars carving gas cavities in NGC 7129

science.title: Supreme Court hearing leaves oil companies’ climate liability cases uncertain
science.summary: Supreme Court justices gave no clear indication how they will resolve oil companies’ effort to stop Boulder, Colorado, from pursuing climate-damages claims in state court. Arguments on Oct. 5 focused on whether federal law preempts the claims and whether the court should intervene before the case reaches trial. ExxonMo
science.content: Supreme Court justices gave no clear indication how they will resolve oil companies’ effort to stop Boulder, Colorado, from pursuing climate-damages claims in state court. Arguments on Oct. 5 focused on whether federal law preempts the claims and whether the court should intervene before the case reaches trial. ExxonMobil and Suncor say the lawsuit would let local courts set energy policy for emissions and fuel sales worldwide; Boulder says it seeks compensation for alleged public deception, not a ban on producing or selling fossil fuels. Justices questioned both the scope of Boulder’s theory and the companies’ argument that the case should be barred, while Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson questioned whether the appeal was premature. The ruling could affect more than 30 similar lawsuits, some of which are paused pending the decision. Justice Samuel Alito’s recusal leaves eight justices to decide; a tie would leave in place the Colorado ruling allowing the case to proceed. A decision is expected in June or July 2027.
science.image_alt: Supreme Court hearing leaves oil companies’ climate liability cases uncertain

science.title: NASA plans bulk rocket purchases for $30 billion lunar base
science.summary: NASA is preparing to buy launch vehicles in bulk for a planned $30 billion permanent lunar base. The agency is seeking a range of rockets to carry cargo as launch demand rises and SpaceX has stopped accepting some Falcon 9 bookings for flights after 2028. NASA says it is seeking alternatives early to avoid a shortage o
science.content: NASA is preparing to buy launch vehicles in bulk for a planned $30 billion permanent lunar base. The agency is seeking a range of rockets to carry cargo as launch demand rises and SpaceX has stopped accepting some Falcon 9 bookings for flights after 2028. NASA says it is seeking alternatives early to avoid a shortage of launch capacity. The plan includes robotic landers and rovers to scout lunar sites and resources, followed by heavy deliveries of equipment for power systems and habitats. NASA also aims to have a lunar reactor ready for launch by December 2030; Russia and China have discussed a separate reactor project with a 2036 target. NASA's proposed reactor would provide power during lunar nights, when solar panels cannot generate electricity.
science.image_alt: NASA plans bulk rocket purchases for $30 billion lunar base

sports.title: Liverpool face Jacquet fitness test before Manchester City visit
sports.summary: Liverpool are waiting to learn whether centre-back Jérémy Jacquet can play against Manchester City at Anfield on Sunday, after France reported a left-leg strain and left him out of the team’s 4-1 win over Belgium. Jacquet has appeared in all seven of Liverpool’s matches this season and started six alongside Virgil van
sports.content: Liverpool are waiting to learn whether centre-back Jérémy Jacquet can play against Manchester City at Anfield on Sunday, after France reported a left-leg strain and left him out of the team’s 4-1 win over Belgium. Jacquet has appeared in all seven of Liverpool’s matches this season and started six alongside Virgil van Dijk. Liverpool also have fitness doubts over forwards Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo: Sweden sent Isak home after one match with a thigh problem, while Gakpo returned from Netherlands duty with an ankle injury. Manchester City lead the Premier League by three points over Arsenal and have appealed the commission’s findings against them in 114 of 115 financial-rule cases. Liverpool defender Milos Kerkez said his side must be at its best to win; Jacquet’s condition will be assessed after he returns to the club.
sports.image_alt: Liverpool face Jacquet fitness test before Manchester City visit

sports.title: India appoints Smriti Mandhana captain after Harmanpreet Kaur steps down
sports.summary: India named opener Smriti Mandhana captain of its women's cricket team across formats on October 6, after Harmanpreet Kaur resigned from the all-format role she had held since 2023. sports.content: India named opener Smriti Mandhana captain of its women's cricket team across formats on October 6, after Harmanpreet Kaur resigned from the all-format role she had held since 2023. Kaur, 37, will continue playing. She led India to its first women's ODI World Cup title last year and a second consecutive Asian Games gold, but questions about her leadership intensified after India's second straight T20 World Cup group-stage exit in June. Mandhana, 30, takes charge having previously led India in 18 T20 internationals and four ODIs, and having won two Women's Premier League titles as Royal Challengers Bengaluru captain, in 2024 and 2026. She called the appointment a "very special honour". Kaur said she was leaving the captaincy believing the team was "in a good place," and that she was ready to play for the love of the game again. The change followed a BCCI review meeting in Guwahati attended by Kaur, Mandhana, coach Amol Muzumdar and secretary Devajit Saikia. India's next assignment is a home series against Zimbabwe, with three T20 internationals and three ODIs scheduled from October 16.

sports.content: Martin O’Neill has confirmed he will remain Celtic manager after considering his future during the international break, saying he is ready to lead the team and pursue the Scottish Premiership title. The 74-year-old had raised the possibility of stepping aside after Celtic lost three straight games: 3-0 to Rangers in the League Cup, 3-1 to Ferencvaros in the Europa League and 1-0 to Rangers in the league. O’Neill said he had reviewed what he had and had not done, and argued that small moments affected some of the defeats. Celtic resume their campaign away to Motherwell on Sunday and lead the league by two points over Rangers.

sports.content: The San Diego Padres beat the Milwaukee Brewers 4-3 in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday, cutting Milwaukee's lead to 2-1 and avoiding elimination. Jake Cronenworth's fifth-inning homer restored San Diego's lead, and Michael King—two days after starting Game 2—pitched the final two innings. Xander Bogaerts ended the game with a double play after King walked two batters in the ninth. San Diego built a 2-0 lead in the third, but Milwaukee tied the game in the fifth before Cronenworth's homer. An error helped the Padres add a sixth-inning insurance run; the Brewers pulled within one in the seventh, then had two runners on with one out in the ninth before Bogaerts turned the game-ending double play. Closer Mason Miller was unavailable after going on the postseason paternity list shortly before first pitch. Game 4 is scheduled for Wednesday, Oct. 7, at Petco Park. Neither team had announced its starter after Game 3; if Milwaukee wins, it advances, while a Padres win would send the series to a decisive Game 5 in Milwaukee on Friday.

sports.content: World No. 1 Jannik Sinner will miss the rest of the 2026 tennis season to undergo treatment for inflammation in his right knee, ending a campaign that stopped after his Wimbledon title in July. Sinner's team said the treatment will allow him to recover before preparing for 2027; the decision rules him out of the ATP Finals in Turin and the Davis Cup finals in Bologna. Sinner said he needed to consider his long-term career and aimed to return fully fit. His absence puts Alexander Zverev in position to take the year-end No. 1 ranking: Sinner is 1,280 points ahead in the live standings but has 3,050 points to defend, compared with 980 for Zverev. The 25-year-old finishes 2026 with a 44-3 singles record and six titles, including five consecutive Masters 1000 victories from March to May.

sports.title: IOC names seven nations in 2036 Olympic host race
sports.summary: The International Olympic Committee has confirmed that seven countries are in discussions to host the 2036 Summer Olympics: Germany, Hungary, India, Qatar, South Korea, South Africa and Turkey. India and Qatar are among the countries seeking their first Olympics, while South Africa could become the first African host.
sports.content: The International Olympic Committee has confirmed that seven countries are in discussions to host the 2036 Summer Olympics: Germany, Hungary, India, Qatar, South Korea, South Africa and Turkey. India and Qatar are among the countries seeking their first Olympics, while South Africa could become the first African host. The IOC will assess plans for venues, athlete experience, financing, public and political support, delivery capacity and long-term legacy. The candidates will present their projects to the IOC’s Future Host Commission in November. The process continues with feasibility assessments by March 2027, a more focused dialogue with preferred candidates in late 2028 and a host vote expected in summer 2029. Other countries have until October 31, 2026, to register interest. Proposals include an Indian bid centered on Ahmedabad and a South African plan spread across Cape Town, Durban and Johannesburg. Qatar is viewed as a leading contender, but a Doha Games would need to take place outside the traditional July-August period because of the heat.

sports.title: Premier League rivals seek multi-year sanctions after Manchester City verdict
sports.summary: Premier League executives are pressing for Manchester City to face penalties covering both past seasons and future competition if the club’s appeal fails, including sanctions lasting beyond a single season of relegation. An independent commission found that City breached financial rules from 2009-10 through 2017-18; Ci
sports.content: Premier League executives are pressing for Manchester City to face penalties covering both past seasons and future competition if the club’s appeal fails, including sanctions lasting beyond a single season of relegation. An independent commission found that City breached financial rules from 2009-10 through 2017-18; City deny wrongdoing and have appealed. No punishment has been announced, and the appeal will be considered separately from a sanctions hearing. Some club executives argue for points deductions over several seasons and transfer restrictions across multiple windows to prevent City from returning quickly to the top flight. Jamie Carragher has separately called for a three-to-five-year punishment, saying a one-season penalty would allow players to endure the consequences and return. A new three-person appeal panel will review the original decision rather than rehear all the evidence. League rules set a 12-week deadline for the hearing and require a ruling within 30 days afterward, although the schedule could be extended. UEFA says it will wait for the Premier League process to finish before deciding whether to act.

sports.content: Novak Djokovic won his seventh China Open title in Beijing on October 6 after Alex de Minaur retired injured in the final. Djokovic took the first set 7-6(3), then trailed 0-1 in the second when de Minaur, who had a medical timeout and a heavily strapped left thigh, stopped with an adductor strain. The 102nd tour-level title extended Djokovic’s unbeaten China Open record to 34 matches and made him the first man to win at least one singles title in 21 consecutive seasons. He is now one title behind Roger Federer’s Open Era total of 103; Jimmy Connors leads with 109. Djokovic said he had endured physical and health problems this year, and called the trophy especially meaningful. The Beijing final followed semifinals that both ended early: Medvedev was disqualified, while Hurkacz retired injured. The wider Asian swing brought other notable developments: Carlos Alcaraz won the Japan Open, and Jannik Sinner’s team said a knee treatment plan would keep him out for the rest of 2026. Djokovic’s Beijing result also improved his position in the race for the ATP Finals.
